links.title: Clear EB filter
links.tooltip: Reset the EB drill-down filter back to all EBs

list.name: voterId
list.label: seat filter
list.description: Regex matched against the committee seat index. Leave at .+ for every seat; type an index such as 44, or an alternation such as 44|91, to narrow. This is a free-text regex rather than a dropdown because the seat set is large and is reassigned every epoch, so a list of values would be stale as often as it is useful. An empty box matches nothing.

list.name: ebWindow
list.label: Recent EB window
list.description: Lookback for the tally growth and announcement lateness panels, so they show recent EBs instead of every EB in the dashboard range. Note that 3h puts the per-EB panel near the Loki 500 series limit.

list.name: threshold
list.label: Certification threshold
list.description: The Leios quorum in force, read from the vote_threshold gauge rather than hardcoded, so the margin, near-miss, shortfall and time-to-certify panels follow a protocol parameter update instead of assuming 0.75. Sourced once here because those panels interpolate it into LogQL, where a label cannot be compared against another label and the value has to be a literal. Blank if leios_voting_process is not deployed, in which case those four panels have no threshold to compare against.

list.name: tallyInstance
list.label: Tally source node
list.description: Single node whose tally stream feeds the seat-counting panels. Every node observes nearly the same votes, so the choice rarely matters, but switch it to cross-check a surprising number against another perspective. Only nodes emitting the tally trace are listed.

list.name: rbHash
list.label: rbHash filter
list.description: Regex matched against the announcing ranking block hash, which identifies one endorser block. Leave at .+ for every EB; paste a hash, or a distinctive prefix, to pin the tally and arrival panels to a single one. Free text rather than a dropdown because this is roughly one value per block, so indexing it would be unbounded and listing it would be enormous. An empty box matches nothing.

panels.title: Certification margin — how close did each EB get?
Certified EBs in range
panels.description: Distinct EBs that reached a certificate in the range. Counted by rbHash rather than by line, since every node that certifies traces it and a raw line count would scale with fleet size. Cross-checks against the margin panels: it should equal the number of EBs whose peak tally crossed the threshold, though it can read higher over ranges longer than the tally stream has existed. Zero means nothing certified in the window.

targets.expr: count(sum by (rbHash) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node", instance=~"$instance", kind="LeiosCertified"} | json rbHash="rbHash" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" [$__range])))

panels.title: Best peak tally
panels.description: Highest tally any single EB reached in the range. Compare against the 0.75 threshold.

targets.expr: max(max by (rbHash) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",tally="tally" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | unwrap tally [$__range])))

panels.title: Mean peak tally
panels.description: Mean across EBs of each EB peak tally. This is the honest headline next to the best-peak tile: the best EB can sit on the line while the typical one is well below it. For the full distribution rather than one number, use the margin table and sort it ascending on shortfall.

targets.expr: avg(max by (rbHash) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",tally="tally" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | unwrap tally [$__range])))

panels.title: Mean shortfall to threshold
panels.description: The threshold minus the mean peak tally. This is the weight that would have to be recovered to certify the typical EB. Zero or negative means the average EB is certifying.

targets.expr: $threshold - avg(max by (rbHash) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",tally="tally" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | unwrap tally [$__range])))

panels.title: Reachable weight observed
panels.description:
Sum of the seat weights of every seat seen casting a vote in the range, derived from the LeiosVoteAcquired weight field rather than from db-sync. Compare with the 0.75 threshold: if this sits at or below it, no EB can certify even with perfect diffusion.

Fixed 1h window, not the dashboard range, and that is load bearing. Seats are reassigned every epoch, so voterId is a rank rather than an identity: aggregating seat weight across an epoch boundary picks each index's heaviest occupant and inflates the total. The inflation grows with the window and there is no gap or error to signal it, so any range near or beyond one epoch reads high and silently.

targets.expr: sum(max by (voterId_x) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",voterId_x="vote.voterId",weight="weight" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | unwrap weight [1h])))

panels.title: Observable participation
panels.description:
Share of the seats known to vote that actually voted in the visible range. Near 100% is the healthy state.

Set the rbHash variable to a single hash and this becomes turnout for that one ranking block.

Two things look like a drop but are not. During an idle hour of the load generator duty cycle no EBs are produced, so this blanks across every seat at once rather than falling for a subset. And seats that have never voted appear in neither number, so a permanently silent cohort is invisible here and this reads high; leios_committee in db-sync is the only source for the true committee size.

Saturates as the range approaches the fixed 24h window the denominator covers. Both numbers read voterId out of the line body, so they count seats seen voting rather than seats seated.

targets.expr: count(sum by (voterId_x) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",voterId_x="vote.voterId" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" [$__range])))
count(sum by (voterId_x) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json voterId_x="vote.voterId" [24h])))

panels.title: Best EB tally in flight (rolling)
panels.description: The highest tally any EB has reached at each point in time, as one series. This is a rolling envelope, not one point per EB: at every step it reports the best of whichever EBs are currently in flight, so it rarely dips and hides how the typical EB did. Use it to see whether anything at all is near the threshold, and the per-EB panel for the distribution. The y axis uses soft bounds of 0.60 to 0.80, so it stays zoomed on the region that matters but expands on its own during a genuine lull rather than clipping one. The dashed line is the certification threshold.

targets.expr: max(max by (rbHash) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",tally="tally" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | unwrap tally [$__auto])))

panels.title: Closest EBs to certification (top 10)
panels.description: The 10 EBs that came closest without certifying, newest first, so a time trend in the near-miss set is visible. Certified EBs are filtered out, so no bar can reach the top of its gauge: the gauge spans 0.60 to the 0.75 threshold, and a nearly full bar is a near miss while an empty one sat at or below 0.60. The tally only rises for a given EB, so its last vote is also the one that set the peak. The margin table has the full set including certified.

targets.expr: topk(10, (max by (rbShort) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",tally="tally" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | label_format rbShort=`{{ substr 0 12 .rbHash }}` | unwrap tally [$__range]))) < $threshold)

max by (rbShort) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",tally="tally" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | label_format rbShort=`{{ substr 0 12 .rbHash }}` | label_format ts=`{{ __timestamp__ | unixEpochMillis }}` | unwrap ts [$__range])) and topk(10, (max by (rbShort) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",tally="tally" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | label_format rbShort=`{{ substr 0 12 .rbHash }}` | unwrap tally [$__range]))) < $threshold)

panels.title: EB margin table — peak tally and shortfall
panels.description: Sortable per-EB view, newest first. Shortfall is the threshold minus the peak; sort ascending on it to find the EBs that came closest, which are the ones a diffusion fix would rescue first. The tally only ever rises for a given EB, so the last vote is also the one that set the peak. Click an rbHash to drill into which seats voted on that EB and when. seats voted is how many committee seats voted on that EB as seen from the tally source node; over a wide enough range that query exceeds Loki 500-series limit and the column drops out of the table entirely rather than degrading.

targets.expr: max by (rbHash) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",tally="tally" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | unwrap tally [$__range]))

$threshold - max by (rbHash) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",tally="tally" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | unwrap tally [$__range]))
sum by (rbHash) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" [$__range]))

max by (rbHash) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | label_format ts=`{{ __timestamp__ | unixEpochMillis }}` | unwrap ts [$__range]))

value.title: Drill down: vote arrival by seat

panels.title: Tally growth, recent EBs
panels.description: One ramp per EB from first vote to peak. This panel ignores the dashboard time range and uses the 'Recent EB window' dropdown instead, defaulting to 10m, so it shows the recent handful rather than every EB in the range. EB cadence is bursty, so the count per window varies. Paste a hash into the rbHash filter to isolate one EB, widening the window if that EB is older than it. The shape says a lot: a smooth climb that stops short is a missing-seat problem, a climb that stalls then resumes is diffusion latency.

targets.expr: max by (rbHash) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",tally="tally" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | unwrap tally [$__auto]))

panels.title: Tally update distribution (Mimir histogram)
panels.description:
Every tally update bucketed. Buckets crowd 0.75 on purpose: the question is near miss versus far miss. A band that piles up just under 0.75 with nothing above it is the signature of a certification stall.

The y axis is the tally value; cell values are updates per second rather than counts, because the buckets are read as a rate and differenced against the bucket below. Multiply by 60 for updates per minute. A small decimal is expected and is not a sign of missing data.

targets.expr: sum by (le) (rate(leios_logmetrics_leios_vote_tally_bucket{instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Committee seats — derived from logs, no db-sync needed
Seat weight and activity by voterId
panels.description:
Committee seat weights derived from the tally trace, no db-sync needed. participation is the share of EBs in the range this seat voted on and EBs voted on is its numerator, both taken from the tally source node so neither scales with the number of reporting nodes. weight lost is seat weight times (1 - participation): the weight this seat is entitled to contribute and does not. The table sorts by it so the top rows are the priority list, and the column total in the footer is the weight recoverable without touching stake, which is the figure to compare against the shortfall tile.

Fixed 1h window, not the dashboard range. Seats are reassigned every epoch, so a voterId is a rank rather than an identity and a window spanning an epoch boundary mixes occupants of the same index: the weight column takes the heaviest of them and the vote counts sum across all of them. Both read high, with no gap or error to signal it.

targets.expr: max by (voterId_x) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json voterId_x="vote.voterId",weight="weight" | unwrap weight [1h]))
sum by (voterId_x) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json voterId_x="vote.voterId" [1h]))

sum by (voterId_x) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json voterId_x="vote.voterId" [1h])) / on() group_left() count(sum by (rbHash) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash" [1h])))

max by (voterId_x) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json voterId_x="vote.voterId",weight="weight" | unwrap weight [1h])) * (1 - (sum by (voterId_x) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json voterId_x="vote.voterId" [1h])) / on() group_left() count(sum by (rbHash) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash" [1h])))))

panels.title: Distinct seats voting over time
panels.description: Seats seen in the tally stream alongside the reachable weight those seats carry, on a fixed 30m lookback. A shorter window only counts seats that happened to vote in the last minute or two and sawtooths badly; a longer one starts mixing committees across epoch rotations. A step down that does not recover is a cohort dropping out. An hourly fall to nothing across every seat at once is the load generator idling between duty cycles, not a fault.

targets.expr: count(sum by (voterId_x) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json voterId_x="vote.voterId" [30m])))
sum(max by (voterId_x) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json voterId_x="vote.voterId",weight="weight" | unwrap weight [30m])))

panels.title: Participation ratio per node (cast / scheduled)
panels.description: Every scheduled vote is an EB this node was asked to vote on, so this is the percentage it actually voted on. Counts only, not weight: use the per-node accounting table below for weight contributed. Anything under 100% is votes this cluster was entitled to cast and did not, and the shortfall is usually diffusion timing rather than misconfiguration; the declined-by-reason panel says which. Brief excursions above 100% are expected, since the two counters are rate-averaged independently and a vote scheduled just before a window boundary can be cast just after. Gaps are not bridged: when no votes are scheduled the line breaks rather than drawing a straight segment across the idle period.

targets.expr: sum by (instance) (rate(leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_cast_total{instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (instance) (rate(leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_scheduled_total{instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Declined votes by reason
panels.description: Declines per bar, as counts rather than a per-second rate, which is too small a number to read on these counters. A 2m minimum interval is set because increase() over a shorter window returns no data here. chainTipDoesNotAnnounce means the voter's chain tip had not adopted the announcing RB when its window opened, which is a diffusion timing problem rather than misconfiguration. tooLate means the window closed first.

targets.expr: sum by (reason) (round(increase(leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_declined_total{instance=~"$instance"}[$__interval])))

panels.title: Per-node vote accounting
panels.description: Scheduled, cast and declined per node over the range, sorted by the weight each node fails to contribute. mean seat weight is the lifetime ratio of contributed weight to votes cast, deliberately not windowed: it is a property of the node seats, and increase() over a range longer than a counter has existed extrapolates the partial window out to full width and reads far too high. weight lost/EB is that times the windowed decline fraction, and is comparable to the per-seat column in the committee table. The three count columns use increase(), which extrapolates slightly at window edges, so treat them as accurate to a percent or two rather than exact. The seat column is the voterId this node has voted with in the last 15m, so rows match the committee seat table above. Seats rotate each epoch and the counter for a previous seat lingers, so the filter keeps only the live one; immediately after a rotation a node may briefly show no seat.

targets.expr: sum by (instance) (round(increase(leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_scheduled_total{instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])))
sum by (instance) (round(increase(leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_cast_total{instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])))
sum by (instance) (round(increase(leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_declined_total{instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])))
sum by (instance) (leios_logmetrics_leios_voted_weight_total{instance=~"$instance"}) / (sum by (instance) (leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_cast_total{instance=~"$instance"}) > 0)

(sum by (instance) (leios_logmetrics_leios_voted_weight_total{instance=~"$instance"}) / (sum by (instance) (leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_cast_total{instance=~"$instance"}) > 0)) * (sum by (instance) (increase(leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_declined_total{instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])) / (sum by (instance) (increase(leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_scheduled_total{instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])) > 0))

sum by (instance) (round(increase(leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_cast_total{instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))) / (sum by (instance) (round(increase(leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_scheduled_total{instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))) > 0)
topk by (instance) (1, sum by (instance, voterId) (increase(leios_logmetrics_leios_votes_cast_total{instance=~"$instance"}[15m]))) > 0

panels.title: Tally quantiles against the quorum threshold
panels.description: Where the tally distribution sits relative to the quorum in force. The threshold line is read from the node rather than assumed, since it is a Dijkstra protocol parameter and can move by parameter update; if it separates from the value the histogram buckets were chosen around, those buckets stop straddling it and want widening. A p90 riding just under the line with the median far below is the certification-stall signature.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(leios_logmetrics_leios_vote_tally_bucket{instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate(leios_logmetrics_leios_vote_tally_bucket{instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))
max(leios_logmetrics_leios_vote_threshold{instance=~"$instance"})

panels.title: Accepted votes per seat
panels.description:
Accepted vote rate broken out by committee seat. Seats that flatline while others keep voting are the ones to chase. LeiosVoteAcquired fires once per accepted vote rather than once per arrival, so this is a distinct-vote rate and is not inflated by how many peers delivered each vote.

One series per seat, so narrow it with the seat filter on a large committee. Loki caps how many series a query may return.

targets.expr: sum by (voterId_x) (rate({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json voterId_x="vote.voterId" | voterId_x =~ "$voterId" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Raw tally lines
panels.description: Filtered by the instance, voterId and rbHash variables. Each line carries the adding seat, its own weight, the running tally and the threshold, so a single line is self-contained.

targets.expr: {service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash"

panels.title: Declined votes, most recent
panels.description: The actual NotVoted lines with their reason, for when the counter tells you something changed and you want to see which EBs were skipped.

targets.expr: {service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosNotVoted", instance=~"$instance"} | json

panels.title: Per-EB peak tally over time
panels.description: One point per EB: the highest tally it reached, plotted at the moment it reached it. The dashed line is the certification threshold, so points below it are EBs that never certified and the vertical gap is the weight they were short. A downward drift means the margin is getting worse.

panels.title: Network view — other operators, seen from our nodes
Participation: our seats vs the whole committee
panels.description: Mean share of EBs voted on, for the seats we operate against every seat on the committee. Our cohort is derived from the LeiosVoted trace, which only fires for votes we cast, so it follows seat rotation without any configured list. Each series divides by the EB count from the same node scope as its numerator, so both stay bounded. Note the committee average includes our own seats, so it understates how far third-party seats lag: the true third-party figure is lower than the lower line.

targets.expr: avg(sum by (voterId) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoted", instance=~"$instance"} [30m])) / on() group_left() count(sum by (rbHash) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance=~"$instance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash" [30m]))))

avg(sum by (voterId_x) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json voterId_x="vote.voterId" [30m])) / on() group_left() count(sum by (rbHash) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash" [30m]))))

panels.title: Time to certify
panels.description: For each EB that crossed the threshold, how long from its first vote to the vote that took it over. Measures the margin in time rather than in weight: EBs certifying only at the last moment are fragile even when the final tally looks comfortable. EBs that never crossed are absent by construction, so a short table means few certifications, not a broken query.

targets.expr: min by (rbHash) (min_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",voterId_x="vote.voterId",tally="tally" | label_format ts=`{{ __timestamp__ | unixEpochMillis }}` | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | unwrap ts [$__range])) and on (rbHash) (min by (rbHash) (min_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",voterId_x="vote.voterId",tally="tally" | label_format ts=`{{ __timestamp__ | unixEpochMillis }}` | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | tally >= $threshold | unwrap ts [$__range])))

min by (rbHash) (min_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",voterId_x="vote.voterId",tally="tally" | label_format ts=`{{ __timestamp__ | unixEpochMillis }}` | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | tally >= $threshold | unwrap ts [$__range]))

panels.title: Vote arrival by seat — set the rbHash filter
panels.description: A drill-down for ONE EB. Paste a hash from the EB column of the margin table into the rbHash filter, or click the EB there to jump straight here. Shows when each seat vote for that EB reached the tally source node, earliest first, so a seat that voted very late is distinguishable from one that never voted at all: late seats appear at the bottom, absent seats are missing entirely. With the filter left at its default this aggregates across every EB and is meaningless.

targets.expr: min by (voterId_x) (min_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",voterId_x="vote.voterId" | label_format ts=`{{ __timestamp__ | unixEpochMillis }}` | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | unwrap ts [$__range]))

max by (voterId_x) (max_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash",voterId_x="vote.voterId",weight="weight" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" | unwrap weight [$__range]))

panels.description: Guard and control for the drill-down below. It counts how many EBs the rbHash filter matches: exactly one means a single EB is selected and the table beneath is meaningful, more than one means the filter is still at its default. Clicking anywhere on this panel jumps to the margin table to pick an EB, in either state; the reference to the top control is a pointer, not a second link, since a stat panel has one click action for its whole surface. Clearing from the top control re-runs only the filter-dependent panels rather than reloading the whole dashboard. Note it reads as selected whenever the range happens to contain exactly one EB, which is possible at very short ranges.

targets.expr: count(sum by (rbHash) (count_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", kind="LeiosVoteAcquired", instance="$tallyInstance"} | json rbHash="vote.rbHash" | rbHash =~ "$rbHash" [$__range])))

1.text: EB selected  —  click to change  ·  Clear EB filter button at top to reset

result.text: ⚠  NO EB SELECTED  —  CLICK HERE  to choose one

links.title: Pick an EB in the margin table

panels.title: Announcement lateness vs vote outcome, per EB
panels.description: Each row is one EB: how late its announcement arrived, which pool produced it, and how our seats then responded. This is the direct test of whether late announcements cost votes. Sorted by announcement age, so if the hypothesis holds the declines concentrate at the top. Announcements, scheduling and declines all key on ebHash, so coverage is every announced EB rather than the subset whose ranking-block hash we can resolve. Scheduled and declined counts come from our own nodes, since a node only traces its own vote decisions; on a network where we run everything that is the whole picture. Lookback is the Recent EB window variable rather than the dashboard range, because one series per EB approaches the Loki 500 series limit past roughly an hour.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.5, {kind="LeiosAnnouncementAccepted", instance=~"$instance"} | json ebHash="ebHash",pool="electionPool",age="announcementAgeSeconds" | unwrap age [$__range]) by (ebHash, pool)
